# Pumps Pumps are the primary means of actively moving gases through a [textlink="pipe network" link="PipeNetworks"]. They draw gas in from one side and push it out the other. There are two types of pumps:
Important facts about pumps: - Pumps [color=#a4885c]require power[/color] from a nearby LV cable. - Pumps output gas on the side with the red stripe. - Gas cannot flow backward through pumps, though if preventing backflow is all you need, it is better to use a [textlink="passive gate" link="PassiveGate"]. - Pumps cannot move gases into pipes whose pressure or volume exceeds their [color=#a4885c]limit[/color]. When this happens, they become [color=red]blocked[/color].
Pumps display a colored animation while operating. If there is no gas to pump or the pump is blocked, it displays a flashing [color=red]red[/color] animation. Pumps that are turned off, unpowered, or unanchored display no animation.
## Pressure Pumps Pressure pumps are the most common type of pump. They move gas based on [color=#a4885c]pressure[/color], making them useful for precisely controlling pipe pressure or creating a vacuum.
A pressure pump [color=red]cannot[/color] move gas into a pipe whose pressure is greater than or equal to the pressure configured on the pump.
For example, a pressure pump set to 500 kPa cannot pump gas into a pipe already at 500 kPa.
Pressure pumps can pump up to a maximum pressure of [color=orange][protodata="GasPressurePump" comp="GasPressurePump" member="MaxTargetPressure"/] kPa[/color]. They become [color=red]blocked[/color] if they try to push gas into a pipe above that pressure.
## Volume Pumps Volume pumps are an alternative type of pump that moves gas based on [color=#a4885c]volume[/color].
They are extremely useful for moving large quantities of gas quickly. They can generally reach higher pressures than pressure pumps.
Although volume pumps operate by volume, they become [color=red]blocked[/color] if they try to push gas into a pipe above [color=orange][protodata="GasVolumePump" comp="GasVolumePump" member="HigherThreshold"/] kPa[/color].
